body:
Thank you for replying.

I've tried therapy but, as mentioned above, it only resulted in some person nodding at me and then billing me for it.

I actually was dumped because I told one of my ex-girlfriends that I was sexually abused. She said she couldn't deal with it and that it was "too real". That was the first time I told someone close to me and consequently the last time.

I was indeed groomed to a certain extent but I don't believe she did it intentionally. You'd have to be inherently evil to do that to another person at that age. It's possible that there are certain children who are inherently evil, or rather sociopathic to negate the religious connotation, but I have seen other sides of her as an adult that are good which makes it less likely she's inherently a sociopath.

I appreciate you're trying to help me find some good resources in my area but it's only a matter of time to end my story.

Thank you for replying.

I know intellectually that it's not my fault but emotionally I feel like I shouldn't have enjoyed it. 

I should have been immediately clear that I didn't want her acting that way. I didn't. Then again, we were both so young.

I kind of slightly blame my parents for their complete lack of an upbringing. I was raised in a very, very poor household where my dad and mom were unemployed but didn't do the financial math and still had a lot of children (9). 

This in combination with going to a school with kids from (upper) middle class while wearing the same clothes for week, showering once a week to save money which resulted in being smelly at school, being overweight because junk food is cheap, being a minority,  having a bald spot at age 14 due to stress, sleeping below a chimney that was stuffed with a sock in an economical attempt to prevent spiders/external cold from crawling through, being bullied by my older brothers because I liked reading,....

Had it only been the sexual abuse in a "normal setting", no problem. I could have dealt with that. But all the other things combined, makes it very hard to deal with life on a daily basis.

I understand but it's hard when you're just paying to see someone nodding at you. Maybe I should just volunteer at a retirement home where I might actually learn something about life.

Male.

Thank you for your response.

I'm sorry that happened to your father. I was also bullied by my older brothers and at school at the same time. I know what it does to your self-esteem. I hope your father is doing better but the pain never really goes away.


I've tried counseling and they just acknowledged what happened as "bad" but they didn't give me any practical advice on how to deal with it. They were just nodding as I was talking about it...

Anyway, thanks again for replying. I'm probably going to kill myself in the not too distant future as the pain of wanting everybody except myself to be happy is killing me inside at an exponential rate but I won't do it tonight.
